title: Arthropod Pest Biology, Identification & IPM
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist pathway
Cultivation personnel responsible for advanced arthropod scouting, identification evidence, containment and escalation
prerequisites: Scouting Systems & Diagnostic Reasoning or equivalent advanced diagnostic foundation
evidencePolicy: Pest biology and identification claims are grounded in controlled extension and peer-reviewed sources. Cannabis/hemp-specific threshold and treatment evidence is preserved as limited where the literature is limited; no universal pesticide or action-threshold rule is implied.
assessmentPolicy: Course-specific assessment remains to be built. No pest-management item or course completion can authorize pesticide selection or application.
description: Builds specialist-level arthropod identification and IPM reasoning for major hemp/cannabis and greenhouse pest groups while emphasizing magnification, life-stage evidence, representative scouting, threshold uncertainty, containment and legal/role boundaries.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate major arthropod pest groups using body form, life stage, plant location, feeding evidence, by-products, movement, and appropriate magnification before assigning pest identity.
Compare cannabis aphid, twospotted spider mite, and hemp russet mite biology, injury patterns, detection limits, and confirmation needs without inventing unsupported action thresholds.
Distinguish thrips and fungus-gnat life stages, signs, injury patterns, sampling locations, and common look-alikes using evidence appropriate to greenhouse crop scouting.
Map likely arthropod movement pathways through plant material, people, tools, air movement, growing media, and crop zones and apply authorized containment and sanitation controls.

Document pest-identification confidence, specimen or image evidence, affected scope, unresolved look-alikes, monitoring method, and treatment-authority boundaries in a reconstructable plant-health record.
